name: CUBA

flag.title: The Cuban Flag
flag.note: Blue & white stripes, red triangle, star

lead: Cuba is the biggest island in the Caribbean. Candy-coloured vintage cars rumble past old, crumbling buildings. Music leaks from every doorway. Havana, the capital, is full of dancers. Cuba grows sugar cane and makes world-famous cigars.
geo: Cuba is a long, thin island, 1,200 km from end to end but rarely more than 100 km wide. The Escambray and Sierra Maestra mountains rise in the south-east, wrapped in cloud forest.
Broad plains once grew sugar cane. Cuba has more than 4,000 smaller islets. It also has limestone caves, underground rivers and coral reefs full of fish.
animals: The bee hummingbird is the world's tiniest bird, barely bigger than a bumblebee. The Cuban solenodon is a shrew-like mammal. It has barely changed since the dinosaurs.
Flamingos wade in pink flocks along the northern cays. Cuban crocodiles splash through freshwater swamps and live nowhere else on Earth. Manatees, hawksbill turtles and whale sharks swim offshore.
culture: Son, salsa and rumba were all born in Cuba. Any street corner can turn into a dance floor. Baseball is the national sport.
Meals are hearty: black beans and rice (moros y cristianos), fried plantain and slow-roasted pork. Cigars hand-rolled in the Vuelta Abajo region are thought to be the world's finest.
history: The Taíno people lived on Cuba before Columbus landed in 1492. Spain ruled for nearly 400 years. It built wealth on sugar plantations worked by enslaved Africans.
Cuba broke free from Spain in 1898. In 1959 Fidel Castro's revolution made the island a communist state. That system still governs today.
wows: The bee hummingbird, found only in Cuba, is lighter than a coin.
Cuba sends more doctors abroad than almost any country.
Havana's 1950s American cars still run because imports were banned for decades.
Cuba was once the world's top sugar exporter.
The Monte Iberia eleuth frog is one of the world's tiniest vertebrates.
A 1961 literacy campaign cut the share who could not read from 23% to 4%.
Cuba lies in a hurricane hotspot, but its evacuation system saves lives.

myths.fact: Chicks are grey or white. They turn pink from the shrimp and algae they eat.

myths.myth: Cuba is very far from the USA
myths.fact: Only about 145 km of sea separates Cuba from Florida.
